name: Deep Malachite Green
lede: Deep Malachite Green is a muted mid green with a name borrowed from the copper mineral, found in Ridgway's 1912 color atlas and in a modern table of nature's colors.

sections.title: A name from the atlases
sections.body:
The swatch derives from Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* of 1912, plate XXXII, hue 35'', and from ISCC-NBS block 136, whose modern name is "light green", 5.0 units away [1]. It is a soft, grey-leaning green, lightness 62 and chroma 25, far from the intensity the word *malachite* suggests [1].

The name also appears in a long table of color names in Baty's *Nature's Palette*, pp. 267 and 268 [2]. The mineral itself has its own page: [[malachite]]. For the pigment cousins, compare [[green-earth]] and [[viridian]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: It appears in 63 of 23,781 archive paintings, 0.26 per cent, rarer than 56 per cent of named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 0.5 per cent of 1,674 paintings, 3.3 times the museums' baseline [3]. Gustav Klimt is the most devoted painter, with it in 4 of his 50 works here, 7.3 times the baseline [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a match is a screen color, not a pigment test [3].
